title: BlueQuartz LLM Gateway - Listing & Integration Strategy Workshop
summary: Technical workshop to align on BlueQuartz marketplace listing requirements, on-prem connector design, KMS compatibility, and performance/quantization tradeoffs for Redwood LLM Gateway integration. Covered packaging, helm chart options, telemetry, and certification criteria for listing. Agreed on benchmarks and a pilot timeline.
next_steps: Redwood to share marketplace packaging checklist and helm example by 2026-03-17
BlueQuartz to run initial quantized inference benchmark using Redwood sample harness and share metrics by 2026-03-26
Schedule follow-up performance lab with infra leads week of 2026-03-29
Exchange KMS integration details and sample IAM policy by 2026-03-19
action_items: Jordan Meyers - share packaging checklist + helm example - 2026-03-17
Priya Raman - provide sample benchmark harness and helper scripts - 2026-03-16
Marco Li - run proto benchmark and upload CSV to shared drive - 2026-03-26
Tasha Nguyen - send BlueQuartz KMS auth flow and compliance requirements - 2026-03-19
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Meyers: Alright welcome everyone, thanks for carving out time. I think we'll run about an hour, agenda up front is marketplace listing requirements, onprem connector packaging, and then a short lab plan around quantization and perf.
[00:18] Evelyn Cruz: Thanks Jordan. We're trying to get the BlueQuartz LLM Gateway listed in the major marketplaces, and we want to make sure the README, helm chart, and KMS bits align with Redwood's expectations. We're targetting enterprise customers that need VPC and bring-your-own-KMS.
[00:35] Marco Li: quick note - our platform currently uses a simple sidecar for routing to model endpoints but we want to surface an operator-based install for customers who want onprem.
[00:46] Priya Raman: got it. From Redwood's side the common pattern we've seen that certs/packaging breaks are usually around the helm values and the KMS bindings. We can share a reference helm chart. Our marketplace tests expect a smoke deploy, KMS handshake, and telemetry ping.
[01:05] Tasha Nguyen: on the security side, we need specifics on the KMS integration: do you require KMS to be reachable from the control plane, or can we keep it fully customer-managed in private networks?
[01:20] Samir Patel: Short answer: marketplace listings generally require a control-plane test that validates the authenticate-and-encrypt flow, but Redwood supports a private-only mode where the control-plane does a handshake without persisting keys. That said, the listing CI needs to be able to run a health check; we can mock the KMS in CI.
[01:38] Marco Li: okay, so for BlueQuartz we'd prefer the private-only path. We must ensure the north-south firewall rules don't leak keys.
[01:46] Jordan Meyers: reasonable. We'll document the private-only KMS pattern. We'll also note any runtime permissions the marketplace CI will need for the smoke tests.
[02:02] Evelyn Cruz: On quantization - our product team is worried about accuracy regressions when moving to int8. We want clear guidance on tradeoffs and recommended profiles per model family.
[02:18] Priya Raman: yep—Redwood Optimize gives recommended quantization profiles based on the model family and sequence length distribution. For example, with 2k context Llama-style models we've seen reasonable results with dynamic 4-bit + some per-layer calibration. But docs are noisy—Priya: I can walk you through an example and share a small eval suite.
[02:39] Evelyn Cruz: that'd be great. Also we need to measure p99 latency and cost per 1k tokens for canary customers.
[02:47] Samir Patel: we'll define a bench harness: sample prompts, 95/99/mean latencies, token counts, CPU/GPU configs. Also include KV cache warm vs cold runs.
[03:03] Marco Li: question — does Redwood's runtime support mixed-precision quantization in the onprem distro? We plan to support both A100 and T4 clusters.
[03:13] Priya Raman: yes, the runtime has kernels for mixed precision and quantization-friendly paths. On T4 you'll usually want a 4-bit/8-bit hybrid; A100 can be more aggressive. But we need to instrument perf labs because batch sizes matter.
[03:29] Evelyn Cruz: who from Redwood is the contact for the helm packaging?
[03:33] Jordan Meyers: Priya will be the point for helm and packaging. I'll coordinate the marketplace checklist and legal touchpoints.
[03:39] Tasha Nguyen: speaking of legal, our compliance team asked about audit logs and retention. What does Redwood expect the listing to provide?
[03:50] Samir Patel: listing must expose audit logs via stdout and a persisted sink—most partners integrate with a provided Elastic/CloudWatch sink. We also require an option to enable/mute PII redaction during captu re (sic). We'll share a sample policy.
[04:10] Marco Li: re: telemetry, do you require specific Prometheus metrics?
[04:15] Priya Raman: the checklist has mandatory and optional metrics. Mandatory: request_count, request_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), model_version, error_count, and a health endpoint. Optional: KV cache hit rate, batch_size distribution. We'll send the list.
[04:30] Jordan Meyers: also worth calling out the marketplace packaging needs a canary rollback path, so your helm chart needs a job that can warm the cache and a post-deploy smoke test.
[04:45] Evelyn Cruz: ok that makes sense. For the smoke test we're happy to run the Redwood-provided harness in our CI. We need a sample token and an example prompt set to validate quality.
[04:57] Priya Raman: we'll provide a minimal prompt set that checks generation coherence and a small reranking task to ensure the outputs are sane. Note: don't use customer data for the smoke tests.
[05:08] Marco Li: on the network side, our operator suggests a sidecar for cert management — any cons?
[05:14] Samir Patel: sidecars are fine but more moving parts. Operator gives clearer lifecycle management for upgrades and onprem UAT. For marketplace, operator-based installs tend to pass cert/upgrade scenarios easier.
[05:27] Evelyn Cruz: timeline: our Q2 roadmap wants a pilot with two customers by end of April. Is that feasible?
[05:35] Jordan Meyers: feasible if we get the helm + benchmark harness this week and you run the initial benchmarks early next week. Then we'll schedule the perf lab the week of Mar 29. So April pilot is tight but doable.
[05:47] Tasha Nguyen: compliance checklist—SOC2 attestation required for our customers. Will Redwood's listing copy indicate Redwood's SOC2 status or must the partner surface their own?
[05:58] Priya Raman: the marketplace listing includes both the vendor (BlueQuartz) and Redwood platform compliance blurbs. For private installs the customer will still rely on BlueQuartz's SOC2 + Redwood's platform security. We'll add the required wording templates.
[06:16] Marco Li: action on our side: run a benchmark on a T4 node with 512 tokens, batch sizes 1/4/8, int8 and fp16 baselines. We'll compare p95/p99 and token cost.
[06:28] Priya Raman: perfect. We'll provide helper scripts to collect p95/p99, mem usage, and GPU util. Also script to post metrics to a shared Prometheus instance or a CSV.
[06:40] Evelyn Cruz: any blockers from Redwood to listing?
[06:44] Jordan Meyers: no blockers—mainly docs, helm, KMS sample, and passing the smoke tests. After that it's the CI run for listing cert.
[06:53] Daniel Ortiz: can we get a short how-to for rollback and canary config? our ops team needs that documented.
[06:59] Samir Patel: yes we'll share a canary runbook and best practice for autoscale / emergency rollback values.
[07:06] Jordan Meyers: great. Recap: Redwood to send packaging checklist + helm by Mar 17, Priya will send benchmark harness by Mar 16, BlueQuartz to run proto benchmarks by Mar 26, Tasha to provide KMS flow by Mar 19. Schedule follow-up perf lab for week of Mar 29.
[07:22] Evelyn Cruz: thanks all, this was helpful. We'll sync internally and pick dates.
[07:28] Jordan Meyers: thanks everyone. I'll email the artifacts and the invite for the perf lab.
[07:33] meeting_end: true
